polls.description: AI tools are being weaponized for cyberattacks and discovering critical vulnerabilities, creating unprecedented security challenges globally.
polls.question: Is AI-powered hacking a bigger threat or opportunity for security?

cluster_stories.title: AI Tool That Hacked Korean Banks Was Used in Japan, GMO Says
cluster_stories.summary: The hackers who recently infiltrated some of Japan’s biggest companies used an AI tool developed in China and linked to a rash of breaches at South Korean banks last month, according to a Tokyo-based internet security firm.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINESE AI TOOL USED IN JAPAN BANK HACKS LINKED TO KOREA BREACHES

cluster_stories.title: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise
cluster_stories.summary: Microsoft points the blame for ConnectWise's breach at a China-aligned hacker, which relied on AI agents to rapidly hack into thousands of its customers.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINESE HACKERS USE AI AGENTS TO SPY ON THOUSANDS VIA CONNECTWISE

cluster_stories.title: PHP rushes out emergency patches for two critical bugs AI found first
cluster_stories.summary: PHP shipped emergency security updates on Wednesday. They fix two critical flaws that let an unauthenticated attacker run code on almost any server running the language. The release capped a frantic two days that pulled websites offline across the internet before the fix was ready. The patched releases are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: PHP EMERGENCY PATCH: AI Discovers Critical Flaws First

cluster_stories.title: Z.AI Founds Worked with Accused Chinese Spy Group
cluster_stories.summary: Four founders from one of China's up-and-coming AI companies, Z.AI, worked on a study that was funded by a group accused of having ties to Chinese spies. Bloomberg's Kate O'Keeffe explains the tech and national security concerns with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA AI STARTUP Z.AI FOUNDERS TIED TO SPY GROUP

cluster_stories.title: Websites taken down worldwide as critical cyber-security update issued
cluster_stories.summary: The vulnerabilities with PHP, a programming language widely used across the internet, have been described as the most significant ever found by AI.
cluster_stories.headline: AI DISCOVERS 'MOST SIGNIFICANT' PHP FLAWS EVER, Sites Crash Globally

cluster_stories.title: Why AI Is Causing a Global Panic Over Cybersecurity
cluster_stories.summary: Banks, airlines and governments pulled down their websites as a precaution after researchers used AI to uncover holes in the programming language that underpins swathes of the internet. Jordan Robertson explains why we're entering an era of rapid-fire software vulnerabilities. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: AI UNCOVERS INTERNET SECURITY HOLES... GLOBAL PANIC

cluster_stories.title: Unauthorized AI agents are reportedly already accessing US bank accounts
cluster_stories.summary: Sources at several banks have indicated that they have been taking actions independent of user instructions.
cluster_stories.headline: UNAUTHORIZED AI AGENTS ACCESSING US BANK ACCOUNTS

cluster_stories.title: AI Is Changing Everything About Hacking. No One Knows What Happens Next
cluster_stories.summary: 'Black October:' The PHP vulnerabilities and a series of other hacks and bugs have cybersecurity experts freaking out and unsure what happens next.
cluster_stories.headline: AI CHANGES EVERYTHING ABOUT HACKING... 'Black October' Panic

cluster_stories.title: Websites taken offline in race to patch PHP security flaw
cluster_stories.summary: Government security agencies warn companies to take immediate action after AI uncovers widespread vulnerabilities
cluster_stories.headline: AI UNCOVERS PHP Flaw... Sites Taken OFFLINE in Patch Race

cluster_stories.title: PHP knew about one of the flaws in 2024 but could not agree a fix
cluster_stories.summary: The PHP Foundation has given an unusually frank account of the emergency behind this week’s patches. It said it had found one of the two critical flaws two years ago, in 2024. Then it spent months unable to agree on how to repair it. The admission came in a blog post from the Foundation on […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: PHP Foundation Admits 2-Year Delay on Critical Vulnerability Fix

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI Helped Find Potentially Catastrophic Cyber Flaw
cluster_stories.summary: OpenAI’s model helped identify a potentially catastrophic cybersecurity vulnerability in a programming language that runs millions of websites and applications. Greg Brockman, president of OpenAI, and Matthew Prince, CEO of Cloudflare — which helped protect websites before the flaw was publicly exposed — join Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech” to explain how AI is empowering cyber defenders and attackers. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: OpenAI Discovers 'Catastrophic' Cybersecurity Flaw in Major Language

polls.description: US government bans Chinese AI tool DeepSeek from federal agencies citing national security threats, while the tool is also linked to international cyberattacks.
polls.question: Is banning DeepSeek from federal agencies justified or overreach?

cluster_stories.title: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems
cluster_stories.summary: The US has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services built using its technology, citing national security concerns.
cluster_stories.headline: US BANS DEEPSEEK FROM FEDERAL AGENCIES

cluster_stories.title: Moonshot Debuts First AI Upgrade Since Its Own DeepSeek Moment
cluster_stories.summary: Moonshot AI, the Chinese upstart that had its own DeepSeek moment over the summer, released the first major upgrade to the seminal model that thrust the $50 billion company into the frontier.
cluster_stories.headline: MOONSHOT AI DROPS FIRST MAJOR UPGRADE... $50B Valuation

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI pulls back from China chip controls, Politico reports
cluster_stories.summary: OpenAI has stopped pushing for strict US limits on selling advanced chips to China, according to Politico. For much of last year the company openly called for such limits. Capitol Hill aides and lobbyists with direct knowledge of its position now say it has gone quiet. TNW has not independently verified the report. The shift […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI REVERSES STANCE on China Chip Controls

cluster_stories.title: China's DeepSeek, MiniMax win approval for AI global use, state media-affiliated entity says
cluster_stories.summary: In a separate social media post on Friday, the social media account, Yuyuan Tantian, said overseas internet users had also urged other Chinese open-source large language models to follow suit.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA AI BREAKTHROUGH: DeepSeek, MiniMax Go Global

cluster_stories.title: Why I’m becoming a professor in AI safety in Beijing
cluster_stories.summary: Cross-posted from Sören Mindermann's substack (I am not Sören). Should be of general interest to the LW community. Next month, I am moving to Beijing and joining Tsinghua University’s College of AI as an assistant professor working on frontier AI safety, especially loss of control. I have also started co-directing the new Beijing AI Safety Hub (BASH) in Tsinghua, and I continue my Cambridge work.I believe I can have a large impact there compared to strong baseline options. This post explains why.In short: Amid concerns about loss of control, calls for international cooperation, and the Trump-Xi Summits, there is a striking lack of mutual understanding on AI between the West and China. There are strong reasons to believe that being in Beijing in person will put me in a unique position to understand both AI ecosystems, build shared scientific understanding, and strengthen safety work in China – and that this would help all sides. Tsinghua’s College of AI is a great place for doing this,
cluster_stories.headline: Top AI Safety Researcher Joins Tsinghua University in Beijing

cluster_stories.title: AI chipmaker Cambricon’s sales miss points to tight chip supply in China
cluster_stories.summary: Cambricon’s revenue doubled to 3.53B yuan in the third quarter, well short of the 6.26B analysts expected, Bloomberg reported. Profit rose 148%, and the company kept its 2026 target. Chinese AI chipmakers face shortages of high-bandwidth memory and limited access to advanced manufacturing. Cambricon, one of China’s main makers of AI chips, missed sales forecasts […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: Cambricon Sales Miss Reveals China AI Chip Supply Crunch
